claims.claim: **At lower doses most NSAID overdoses are benign.** ⚠️ **A large overdose can lead to coma, shock, seizures and acute renal failure.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mefenamic acid overdose is associated with seizures — over 3.5 g can cause them.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Covers** ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, celecoxib, meloxicam, indomethacin, ketorolac, piroxicam, etoricoxib, parecoxib, mefenamic acid, ketoprofen, sulindac, tiaprofenic acid — **not aspirin** (see salicylate poisoning).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** any symptomatic child · any significant accidental ingestion or deliberate self-poisoning. **Consider non-accidental poisoning** if developmental age doesn't fit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for:** epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting · drowsiness, lethargy, seizures, coma · acute renal failure · shock.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ibuprofen severity:** under 200 mg/kg no symptoms · 200–400 mg/kg mild CNS and GI effects · ⚠️ **over 400 mg/kg multi-organ dysfunction becomes a risk.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptomatic or concurrently ill children: FBC, UEC, LFTs.** Consider paracetamol in all intentional overdoses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Care is supportive. After a large overdose, keep the child well hydrated** to lower the risk of acute renal failure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with a toxicologist**, particularly for symptomatic children and abnormal pathology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Epigastric pain → proton pump inhibitor; seizures → manage as afebrile seizures.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admit for observation:** all symptomatic children · ⚠️ **ibuprofen 200 mg/kg or more** · all intentional overdoses. Poisons Information Centre 131126.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** when care exceeds the local centre's capacity. PIPER: 1300 137 650.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A child who is symptom-free with normal vital signs can go home 4 hours after ingestion.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adolescents with deliberate ingestion need a self-harm risk assessment and drug and alcohol assessment before discharge**, with links to services if needs are found.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug NSAID poisoning' (Last Updated April 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nonsteroidal_Anti-inflammatory_Drug_NSAID_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
